chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what the limit of ruku' and sajdah is?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent, and to His praise, three times in ruku', and Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, and to His praise, three times in sajdah. Whoever misses one, a third of his prayer is missed; whoever misses two, two-thirds of his prayer is missed; and whoever does not glorify, he has no prayer.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If he leaves the tashahhud out of forgetfulness, he makes it up and does not repeat the prayer.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High (recited in sujood)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent (recited in ruku)
key_terms.قَضَاهُ: He makes it up (completes the missed part)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for ruku and sujood to validate the prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the minimum threshold for valid bowing and prostration as three recitations of the specific glorifications, linking the completeness of the prayer directly to the consistency of these devotional acts. This hadith highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while the prayer remains valid with partial omission, the spiritual merit is proportionally diminished, reflecting the balance between legal validity (sahha) and perfection (kamal). The accompanying note from Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that forgetting the tashahhud is a minor error requiring only compensation (qada) rather than a full repetition, distinguishing it from more significant structural omissions.
